text:
Quinn Hughes is playing 28 minutes a night for Minnesota, and lately closer to 29. Over the last ten games his ice time is up more than two minutes, and over the last seven he has a point every night: 4 goals, 8 assists. The Wild have been winning with him logging those minutes, and at five on five they take 60% of the expected goals while he's out there.

There's one part of his line to discount. Hughes has 6 goals on 3.4 expected, shooting 12% after 4% last season. He's never been a shooter first, and our range puts his true rate nearer 6%. The assists are the real currency, and 19 in 18 games is right in his lane: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey rated him the most valuable defenseman in the league in 2025-26, at 4.9 wins above replacement.

Then there's the contract. Daily Faceoff's look at the top 2027 free agents asks, "Does Quinn Hughes make it to market?" Every 30-minute night makes the answer more expensive.
headline: Thirty minutes a night, and a contract year
